title: a-fixme-answer-binds-to-the-kick-back-it-answers
intention: A FIXME answer binds to the kick-back it answers, so an answer written for an earlier kick-back can never satisfy a later kick-back's entry of the same number.
why: Measured 2026-10-08 on 80518446bfc8: kick-back 1 (history seq 23) listed two fixme entries, answered by decisions 11-12 (FIXME 1, FIXME 2); kick-back 2 (seq 26) listed one entry, and decision 11 already satisfied 'FIXME 1' — inspect_fixme matches over every decision the ticket ever carried, so the gate would have passed with nothing answering the second kick-back. Only decision 13, written by discipline, answered it. A hollow pass at a gate.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — the FIXME gate is a proof record, and an answer to a different kick-back is a hollow pass of it) and Law 3 (an entry is not known answered until an answer to THAT entry is measured). Measured 2026-10-08 on 80518446bfc8: kick-back 1 (seq 23, 00:51:59 local) listed 2 entries, answered by decisions 11-12 (FIXME 1, FIXME 2, 07:03 UTC); kick-back 2 (seq 26, 01:56:08 local) listed 1 entry, and decision 11 already satisfied 'FIXME 1' — the gate would have passed with nothing answering kick-back 2 (decision 13 did, by hand discipline only).
how: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.py: inspect_fixme reads the ticket's latest crossing INTO FIXME from the component's history (the record emit already writes: to == 'FIXME', ticket, at) and counts as an answer only a 'FIXME <n>' decision whose `at` is at or after that crossing. No kick-back record found for the ticket is a red, never a pass. emit's FIXME gate passes its history_path through. One new tooth reds when an earlier kick-back's FIXME n answer satisfies a later FIXME n.
falsifier: Falsifier: a new proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_fixme_answer_binds_to_its_kick_back.py, green and sealed under bin/cairn test --netns, teeth under PROVES for this ticket: (1) test_an_earlier_kick_backs_answer_does_not_satisfy_a_later_one — a fixture component crossed into FIXME through emit (with ticket and missing), a 'FIXME 1' decision written after it, then crossed out and back into FIXME again; with fixme list [one entry] and only the old decision, the FIXME gate refuses naming entry 1; (2) test_an_answer_written_after_the_latest_kick_back_admits_it — the same fixture plus a 'FIXME 1' decision stamped after the second kick-back: the gate's lane reads expected == actual; (3) test_no_kick_back_record_is_a_red — a ticket at FIXME with a fixme list and answers, but no crossing into FIXME in the history the gate is given, reds, and so does history_path None; (4) test_the_two_clocks_compare — the kick-back record stamped local naive; a decision one hour EARLIER in true time but written with a +12:00 offset (so its string sorts after the kick-back's) is NOT counted, and one an hour LATER written with a -12:00 offset (its string sorts before) IS counted — string comparison fails both, in any local zone. 72d2f79daf0a's test_fixme.py stays green (fixtures per open-816be0ed2fbc). Teeth 1, 3 and 4 red with transitions.py reverted to the pre-build commit (the hollow). Horizon: this voyage; then the next ticket kicked back twice is measured by the gate rather than by hand.

(C) inspect_fixme(ticket, history_path: str | None = None): after the fixme list is read and non-empty, kick = _latest_kick_back(ticket, history_path); since = _when(kick.get('at')) if kick else None; if since is None: actual = f"ticket {ticket!r} stands at FIXME but no crossing into FIXME for it is recorded in {history_path!r} — which kick-back its answers answer cannot be read" and unanswered = list(range(1, len(fixme) + 1)); else answered is built only from decisions whose _when(d.get('at')) is not None and >= since; the red text adds f" (answers counted from kick-back seq {kick.get('seq')} at {kick.get('at')})". The lane identity every_fixme_entry_is_answered and the code string stay. (D) _fixme_gate(ticket, history_path=None) passes it through; the call at transitions.py:2095 becomes _fixme_gate(journal_extra.get('ticket'), history_path=history_path). (E) the docstring of inspect_fixme says the binding and cites this ticket. For tooth 1 the second kick-back is a second emit into FIXME from the FIXME-standing string after crossing out (or a second back-edge emit from _AT_PROVEME into the same history) — the gate reads only the LAST record. decisions.text: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, directly above def inspect_fixme, add two private functions. (a) def _latest_kick_back(ticket: object, history_path: str | None) -> dict | None: return None when history_path is falsy or os.path.exists(history_path) is false; otherwise walk projector.read_history(history_path) and return the LAST record e with str(e.get('ticket')) == str(ticket) and canon(str(e.get('to', '')), ['FIXME']) == 'FIXME' (canon is already imported from cairn.tools.system_word; its signature is canon(token, table)), else None. (b) def _when(stamp: object) -> datetime | None: try datetime.fromisoformat(str(stamp)); on ValueError or TypeError return None; a naive result (tzinfo None) is local time and is returned as .astimezone(); an aware result is returned as it is. history stamps are naive local (projector.py:222); rehearsal decision stamps are UTC with +00:00 (rehearsal.py:861); comparing the two as aware datetimes is what tooth 4 measures. datetime is already imported.
decisions.step: unlisted: add _latest_kick_back(ticket, history_path) and _when(stamp) to transitions.py above inspect_fixme

decisions.text: Change the signature to def inspect_fixme(ticket: object, history_path: str | None = None) -> list[dict]. Keep expected, code, the lane name every_fixme_entry_is_answered and the two existing early reds (no ticket file; no fixme list) unchanged. In the branch where fixme is a non-empty list: kick = _latest_kick_back(ticket, history_path); since = _when(kick.get('at')) if kick else None. If since is None: unanswered = list(range(1, len(fixme) + 1)) and actual = f"ticket {ticket!r} stands at FIXME but no crossing into FIXME for it is recorded in {history_path!r} — which kick-back its answers answer cannot be read". Otherwise answered = the set of str(d.get('step','')).strip() over decisions d that are dicts with non-empty str(d.get('text','')).strip() AND whose w = _when(d.get('at')) is not None and w >= since (a decision with no readable 'at' is not an answer); unanswered = [n for n in 1..len(fixme) if f'FIXME {n}' not in answered]; actual = expected if not unanswered else f"fixme entries {unanswered} on {ticket!r} have no FIXME <n> decision (answers counted from kick-back seq {kick.get('seq')} at {kick.get('at')})". Return the same single _lane call as today.
decisions.step: unlisted: inspect_fixme(ticket, history_path=None) counts only answers at or after the latest kick-back

decisions.text: def _fixme_gate(ticket: object, history_path: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]: return FIXME_GATE.run(inspect_fixme(ticket, history_path=history_path), note=None). emit already receives history_path as its own keyword parameter (def emit(..., history_path: str | None = None, ...), transitions.py:2011); its one call at transitions.py:2135, fixme_note, _rec = _fixme_gate(journal_extra.get("ticket")), becomes fixme_note, _rec = _fixme_gate(journal_extra.get("ticket"), history_path=history_path). No other caller exists outside the proofs (grep: transitions.py:2135, test_fixme.py:133).

decisions.text: The 'at' stamp is NOT set through emit and touches no history record: emit only writes the kick-back crossing. The decisions are the plain dicts in the fixture ticket body handed to _Corpus, so the stamp is one more key in each literal, e.g. tooth 2's body becomes {"fixme": ["a", "b"], "decisions": [{"step": "FIXME 1", "text": "answered", "at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}]}, built AFTER the kick-back emit returns; tooth 3's two decision dicts gain the same key the same way. The proof's _answer(step, at) helper does the same thing.
